title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck has just treated projective connections on curves of genus 0 with nu holes (previous page). Here he studies translation-invariant projective connections on a torsor X under a smooth group scheme H of relative dimension 1 over S, with 2 invertible.

Local data. By translation everything is determined by data at the origin of H:
- omega_0 = invariant 1-forms, i.e. the cotangent line at the unit section.
- V_0 = a rank-3 bundle of 'linear' or second-order (projective) vector fields, the sl_2-type algebra attached to 2-jets. It carries a filtration omega_0 ⊂ L_0 ⊂ V_0 with graded pieces omega_0, O_S, omega_0^{-1}.
- L_0 = (O_H/J^3)^+, built from 2-jets at the origin, where J is the augmentation ideal.
- P_0 = P(L_0), a P^1-bundle over S with a canonical section sigma_0: the osculating projective line at the origin.

Proposition. Invariant projective connections on X (the text says 'conn. affines'; context indicates projective, or affine-induced) correspond bijectively to sections of a sub-torsor of V_0 ⊗ omega_0 under omega_0^2. This sub-torsor projects onto the section 1 of omega_0^{-1} ⊗ omega_0 = O_S. After a suitable splitting V_0 = omega_0 ⊕ O_S ⊕ omega_0^{-1}, its sections are those of the form a_2 + a_1 + 1. The margin says the right splitting of O_S inside L_0 is given by 2-jets of odd functions, using the inversion x -> -x of the group, which is where 2 invertible enters.

Reformulation. Equivalently, these are sections of P(omega_0 ⊕ omega_0^{-1}) disjoint from the canonical section given by omega_0, i.e. splittings of 0 -> omega_0 -> E -> omega_0^{-1} -> 0. These form a torsor under Hom(omega_0^{-1}, omega_0) = omega_0^2, the invariant quadratic differentials.

The canonical connection. There is a canonical choice, the section 0+0+1, which he calls the Campbell-Hausdorff one. It is the projective connection induced by the invariant affine structure, i.e. the coordinate given by integrating the invariant differential, morally the logarithm of the formal group. It is characterized among invariant projective connections by the existence, locally on S, of a translation-invariant reduction of the structure group of the P^1-bundle P to G_a. The next page phrases this via an invariant extension 0 -> O_X -> F -> O_X -> 0 with P ≅ P(F).

Next page. Over an algebraically closed field, the canonical connection is the unique invariant one whose P has exactly one stable line. Every other invariant one has exactly two stable lines. Concretely, invariant projective structures have constant Schwarzian c·omega^2 with c = -lambda^2/2 and developing map exp(lambda x). For c ≠ 0 the holonomy is semisimple with two fixed points; for c = 0 it is unipotent (affine).

Elliptic case. For H an elliptic curve, every projective connection on X is invariant, since every quadratic differential is invariant. The canonical one is then the uniformization (flat) structure.
errors: The text says the 'conn. affines' are in bijection with the sub-torsor. Given the omega^2-torsor structure and P(omega+omega^{-1}), the objects classified are invariant projective connections. Either this is a slip, or he means projective connections arising from affine ones.

Sections written a_2 + a_1 + 1 would form a torsor under omega^2 ⊕ omega, not omega^2. The component a_1 must be fixed, e.g. to 0 by the odd-jet splitting, for the stated torsor structure under omega_0^2 to hold. The page leaves this implicit.

The 'Campbell-Hausdorff' name for the canonical structure is heuristic. In positive or mixed characteristic no logarithm exists, but the invariant affine connection (invariant differential flat) still gives the algebraic canonical projective connection. So the construction is fine; only the name is characteristic-0 flavoured.

ideas.what: Invariant projective connections on a torsor under a 1-dimensional smooth group scheme form a torsor under invariant quadratic differentials, described at the origin via a filtered rank-3 bundle omega ⊂ L ⊂ V of 2-jets.
ideas.modern_name: translation-invariant projective structures / PGL_2-opers on 1-dimensional groups; Schwarzian torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (projective structures, 1960s); Deligne (Équations différentielles à points singuliers réguliers, 1970); Beilinson-Drinfeld (opers)

ideas.what: A canonical invariant projective connection (from exponential/log coordinates, or the invariant affine structure), characterized by reduction of the structure group to G_a, i.e. unipotent holonomy.
ideas.modern_name: projective structure induced by the invariant (flat) affine connection; parabolic vs hyperbolic invariant projective structures

ideas.what: Over an algebraically closed field, non-canonical invariant projective connections have exactly two stable lines (constant Schwarzian ≠ 0, developing map exp(lambda x)); the canonical one has one.
ideas.modern_name: classification of invariant projective structures by holonomy type (semisimple vs unipotent)

ideas.what: Using the inversion of the group (2 invertible) to choose the splitting via 2-jets of odd functions.

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up projective connections purely algebraically over an arbitrary base (2 invertible) as a filtered rank-3 bundle omega ⊂ L ⊂ V with graded pieces omega, O, omega^{-1}, plus a torsor of splittings. This is essentially the sl_2-oper formalism, and it precedes Drinfeld-Sokolov and Beilinson-Drinfeld. The idea is known in spirit (Deligne 1970), so the novelty is only historical.
missed.quote: V_0 = ω_0 ⊕ O_S ⊕ ω_0^{-1} s'écrivent sous la forme a_2 + a_1 + 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's ca. 1972 jet-theoretic approach to projective connections over general bases, linked to Gauss-Manin and Cartier operator questions. That is of historical interest for the prehistory of opers in mixed or positive characteristic.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but essentially classical material: invariant projective structures on 1-dimensional groups and elliptic curves, a canonical structure from the invariant affine connection, and classification by stable lines. It is phrased in a nice relative-algebraic form anticipating oper language, but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'conn. affines' — likely meant projective connections (or the marginal insertion modifies it); the classification is of invariant projective connections.
'jouissant de Hausdorff [?]' is probably a marginal '(Campbell-)Hausdorff' annotation attached to 'un scindage convenable'.
'qui ne disjoint' should read 'qui sont disjointes' (sections of P(ω_0+ω_0^{-1}) disjoint from the canonical section).
'Alg. de Lie des champs [?] lin. 3' — probably refers to a rank-3 Lie algebra of (projective) vector fields of jet order ≤2; the margin '𝒱(3)' is consistent with this.
The margin reading 'jets d'ordre 2 de fonctions impaires' is plausible and consistent with the use of 2 invertible.
